column2: An infinite recursive zoom (Droste effect, "Powers of Ten"). The picture contains itself; time passes by falling forever inward, and a new minute is found inside the old one.
Russian avant-garde: Rodchenko, El Lissitzky, Stepanova. A kinetic propaganda poster of wedges, bars, circles and diagonals in red, black and cream, with bold slab type and halftone photomontage.
PlayStation-1-era 3D: flat-shaded low-poly geometry, wobbling vertices, warped affine textures, fog, a moving camera. A whole small 3D world on 160x80.
Hundreds of tiny pixel workers, Lemmings-style, with jobs (diggers, builders, climbers, floaters, blockers). The time is something they build, dig or become.
Living generative morphogenesis: reaction-diffusion (Turing patterns), stripes and spots that grow, split, flow and heal. Nature computing the time.
Not digits: a new way to read the time, in the spirit of Urwerk wandering hours or Ressence. A celestial or mechanical system whose positions are the time.
Surrealist painting, Magritte-style: a calm, impossible scene with crisp painted light (a day sky over a night street, a bowler hat, a floating rock, a pipe). The time hides in the impossibility.
A tiny retro computer desktop (1-bit early Mac, Windows 95, or something stranger) that is alive: windows, cursor, dialogs, progress bars, a screensaver. The OS itself tells the time.
